note: The public Known gaps page (/restoration/gaps/): which gaps players see, in our own plain words. id is a coverage register row (G...) whose State the builder reads, or our own id (F... being fixed, P... on purpose) for items with no row. show: lost (no source survived; a fix still wins), purpose (a deliberate difference; always shown as On purpose), fixing (being fixed; commits, once landed, turn it into Fixed). commits: game:, site: or server: hashes that fix it, when the register row cites none. Never a player's name, a quote from a player, a file path or an em-dash. tools/gaps/build-data.mjs writes public/restoration/gaps.json from this.

gaps.text: Most of Glitch's private quest rooms and Jethimadh Tower rooms left no map behind. Each one is rebuilt by hand from players' recordings and snaps, and some may never come back.
The EZ Cookin' practice street and the Talking 'bout Soil Appreciation room are not built yet, so those quests play without their rooms.
On the Winter Walk you cannot knock the icicles down yet.
The Winter Walk's motes no longer come back when you leave the walk, and they pay Glitch's amounts.
Stepping into a quest room from the Ancestral Lands pauses the visit timer, as Glitch did.
Chasing Hubba Dubba Hugs is offered but cannot be finished, and Tend to Your Community never ticks its Herb Gardens step.

The counters on Sparkly of Interest and Another Simple Sample never move, some quest timers keep running while you are away, and Walk Toward the Light opens at a level instead of after Glitch's upgrades.
A few quest reward lines show a fixed amount instead of what was really paid.
A few named streets, such as Celestial Strum and Coulcairn, have no map and no layout anywhere we have found.
In Thornfad Layers, the letter or heart that shows over your head by the locked door is not drawn yet.
The herb gift on five streets is still to come; Ding a Lingers waits on the snow roads.
Teleporters that work by walking into them have not all been checked yet.
A few items have no picture of their own when dropped on the ground yet.
Mokkar Mill shows only one of its seven Jellisacs.
Jellisacs and Peat Bogs stand where the 2012 snaps show them, and every Herb Gardens planter box is an herb bed.
The small dark figure on the Hell Bar's counter, and the bar's own music, are still unidentified.
Unused Tiny Speck animations are in: Chickens peck and pause, potions pour from their own bottles, and tools show at the rocks and barnacles you work.
There is no world map or subway map view yet, and GO buttons do not take the colour of the region they lead to.
Some of Glitch's sounds and tunes were never archived anywhere, so they play a simple stand-in.
An early take of Esquibeth's waterfall song has no surviving copy.
Short lines from animals and characters stay up for Glitch's own times, such as three seconds for a Yum!
Where Glitch put the Qurazy quoin markers was never archived, so each street picks its own spot.
Quoins in races, puzzle rooms, the Purple journey and the winter motes still pop with a short float instead of Glitch's full burst.
Rainbow Run and Top of the Tree quoins vanish without paying once you reach the daily quoin limit.
A few dozen items in the encyclopedia have no icon, because their art was never archived.
Rare items from the Penalty Box shop are not numbered and do not stay tied to their first owner yet.
Some house styles are still to come, including more interior and back yard styles.
The name sign on a player tower and the lettering of its floor numbers have no free source, so they look different from Glitch.
Visitors see the owner's Garden Gnomes, Magic Sticks and animal machines on a home street.
A key-holder walking into another player's house no longer gets a page error.
The donation window opens at a useful amount, as Glitch's did, instead of at 1.
An open bag no longer covers the donation window.
The favor display stays up when any Giant has your favor, so the Favor with the Giants panel can be opened from anywhere.
The donation that fills a Giant's favor gives no emblem, later donations use up the day's limit for nothing, and there is no warning before you go over it.
Favor filled outside a donation gives no prompt to collect the emblem, and some favor can go past the cap.
Street projects never ask how many to give, and online helpers from an earlier phase get no completion card or reward.
Work stops when you walk a short way off, the panel shows no rewards or leaderboard, and some refusals show raw names.
Cultivation Nurturer, Restorer of Stuff and Make Do and Mender cannot be earned.
Talking to a Street Spirit opens its street project, as in Glitch.
A plain Pick can mine Metal Rock, dragging a Pick onto a rock wears a different pick, and Rubeweed does not raise the gem chance.
Online, only the first of two players on one rock or node is paid, and Ice has no Help scrape.
Picks, Shovels and Scrapers have no verbs in the pack, and the Tinkertool cannot repair itself or mend a tool bit by bit when it is worn.
Harvesting a tree with exactly the energy it costs can croak you, and street Wood Trees never grow back after chopping.
Street fruit trees never grow bigger, and a tiny Wood Tree does not warn that harvesting will clear it.
Garden potions ask for far too much energy, a plot that is still a little wet cannot be topped up, and pouring on a shared Master Garden can say you are too tired when you are not.
Chickens squawk and flutter off when you walk into them.
Reviving a rooked animal counts the real helpers, and a party invite stays up while you eat to get your energy back.
In solo you can squeeze a Chicken that is sitting on your egg, and Super Animal Harvest does not give its Bacon chance.
Drinks give the same iMG whatever your mood, you can drink while dead and lose the drink, and a Rasher of Bacon cannot be eaten.
Buffs keep running while the game is closed and can vanish on reload without their end effect.
Making pays iMG with no daily limit per recipe, and every Test Tube mix is known from the start instead of found by experimenting.
Meditation can say you gained energy right after saying you are too pooped, and a short first session can stick the Meditation Station.
Levelling up while Super Pooped or dead refills you, the Energy Tank card fills energy but not mood, and online nobody hears that you levelled up.
The Faded Heart's Remember counts haunts on streets that have none, and hints at a later story that does not exist.
Teleporting works out its energy cost from a 100-energy tank, and you cannot save a Teleportation Point in your own home.
Teleportation V cannot summon a player into a home yet.
Teleportation V can summon another player to your street or your Party Space.

A few messages point to the wrong place: retrying Gwendolyn's Task or Rainbow Run, joining a Party Space later, skipping the tutorial online, and teleporting from the Map before you have the rank for it.
Some lines the characters say are still in our own words while the original lines are checked.
A note left on the ground stays private to you. In Glitch anyone could read it.
Appear offline still shows you to players on the same street.
A neighbour's note can say they have not read yours right after they replied.
A summons or invite can be answered while a quest card is open.
On some phones, big streets can still use too much memory and close the game. A lighter mode for phones is planned.
Zoomed in on a phone, your Glitch sits high in the view.
A second finger on the movement stick moves it.
Some tips still name keys a phone does not have, such as Space to float higher or to fly in Paradise.
On a phone you can pinch the street to zoom, scroll the pack row and tap signpost arms.
In Classic, the Wardrobe is not its own window yet, and new players do not get the 2012 arrow picker for their look.
You cannot rename your own character yet. An administrator can do it for you.
The character card can miscount a retired character, and a blocked sign-up says to try again tomorrow when the wait is longer.
After a failed restore of a backup, the solo game could stop saving until you reloaded.
Wood Trees take care only once a game day, so a planted one needs days of real time to grow.
Rocks stand lower than the 2012 snaps show them, in one shape, and some planned things hang over ledge ends or sit on steep slopes.
Teleporting and /stuck do not work inside a quest room, where Glitch let you leave that way.
Seeker of the Shiny and Meditation Station are offered again every 5 minutes until you take them.
On an iPhone the game could close itself on the way into some streets, such as Froughtful Fen.
Pinching to zoom on a phone flickered black, and the closest zoom was blurry.
On a phone, Cultivate, Decoration Mode and some windows such as Groups, Account and Auctions did not fit the screen, so some choices and close buttons were out of reach.

On a phone the upgrade cards, the Imagination screen, Make, the Map, Mail, the pack row, the loading card and the report window were cramped or partly off the screen, and the top bar did not show currants or favor.
The phone page's Mail count included letters already read and archived.
A Still worked only from the pack and did nothing once dropped, where Glitch had it work on the ground with its own animations.
A juice picked in a machine's Make window could go uncounted for quests, and a machine gave no reason when it could not start.
In the Juju Hideout the campfire and a chair floated above the ground.
The community boards' sign-in had no Continue with Google, though the game's has one.
Camera Mode could not be opened on a phone, which has no keyboard.
Players could not see their own reports' numbers.
A street project that asked for the same item twice put what you gave on the first row, whichever row you used.
Online, a street you could already walk to showed its project as built while the world had not finished it, so you could not help.
With a full pack, the drink ticket went to your Magic Rock without saying so, and the Bartender's wine followed it unseen.
With a full pack, claiming an emblem said more favor was needed instead of asking for room in the pack.
In the Tower's Ventilation Room you walked out over thin air instead of dropping down the shaft.
In the Museum of the Rook the Greeterbot greeted you from out of sight.
In the gut tubes a phone's Jump button did not flip which way is down, so a phone player could get stuck.
Enter could not reach things resting on a counter or table beside you, such as the food in EZ Cookin'.
The street map in the corner showed a rough sketch while a street's art loaded.
A game link opened on a phone lost its settings on the way through the phone page.
The Magic Rock's card showed before the rock's white glow.
Notices covered the featured project's progress under the street name.
In Classic, buff and cooldown chips sat on the energy arc.
An open bag closed when you clicked away, so you could not watch its counts while collecting.
A vendor's shelf jumped back to the top after each sale.
In Classic, a long Menu ran off the window, so Sign out could be out of reach.
Online, the featured project still refused your work on a street you had already walked onto, saying the street was already built.
A Meat Collector, Butterfly Milker, Piggy Feeder or Magic Sticks refused in the house's yard said they only work in a back yard, without naming the home street where they do.
A Make window's Show them listed every recipe, not the ones you know, and never said what each was missing.
New quests counted in the Quests panel could not be found in its tabs.
In Classic, Pin to screen did nothing you could see.
On Winter Walk at the daily coin limit, the motes refused you without a word.
Street crabs were drawn smaller than in Glitch, so their dance was hard to see.
A subway ride played two tunes over each other.
A game left open across an update said you were too far from rocks and trees you stood beside, without saying a reload fixes it.
Some rocks, peat bogs and paper trees hung above their ground, so you had to jump to use them.
A conversation card sat over the character talking to you.
A Storage Display Box squashed its item's picture into a square.
The top line over a picked-up Musicblock vanished too fast to read.
Scraping a barnacle, digging a dirt pile and cutting peat played their tool sound after the work instead of during it.
Milking a butterfly that was not ready ran its answer across the whole screen in one line.
Legalize It's Bureaucratic Hall had no way out: its glass doors were missing.
A vendor could buy the units your Magic Rock held for a full pack, along with the stack in your pack.
A meditation cut short by a teleport did not count on the street it started on.
The Louise Pasture Villa's door stood alone in an open field, with no house around it.
Groddle Meadow's shrines stood far from where Tiny Speck's 2012 street pictures show them.
In Radiant Glare, the top bank of bulbs refused clicks from the disc, though the room said clicking works from anywhere.
A shrine, tree, vendor or animal could stand on top of a Peat Bog, Jellisac or Barnacle.
Joining a street with a felled tree drew its Patch twice.
With a bag open, a quest's award waited, so Gwendolyn's Task never offered its second part.
A Swoonerfly lying on the ground showed no name, so it looked like a dying butterfly.
Legalize It sent you to a private copy of the Bureaucratic Hall, so you could not see other players there as you could in Glitch.
Shrines in sixteen regions stood where the game guessed, often far from where Tiny Speck's 2012 street pictures show them.
An Autumn Day played its own music only once, over the usual street music.
A recipe that needed an achievement or a skill named it without a link to see what it takes.
On a small phone a cabinet's storage window scrolled sideways.
A save that failed did so without a word, and a game page left open across an update could save over the newer version's save.
On some Android phones the Meal Vendor and Helga turned into black squares.
The myopic frog asked its question before you could use Camera Mode; in Glitch the first talk was only the introduction.
The Firebog, Groddle and Uralia Street Spirit cubimals could not be given to the Street Spirits.
Buying an upgrade card could play no sound; Glitch played a fanfare.
The shrine window offered a count for tools, which can only be donated one at a time.
The once-every-42-game-days Piggy capture limit applied in your own house and yards, where Glitch had no limit.
Hispikulus's Amazing Ramble counted too few Qurazy quoins found on new streets.
Butterflies on tall streets said you needed to be closer and then jumped away.
Phones had no way to act on the nearest thing, so signs and animals behind scenery were hard to reach.
It Takes Two did not say that the player being helped is the one whose dig counts.
A few narrow streets, such as Semsan Simile, are shown zoomed in on wide screens.
While a street rested after finishing a project, its signpost still sent you to the Street Spirit, which had nothing to give yet.
In Le Misérable II you could walk through the crawl-space doors before being shrunk.
The Act chooser showed blank tiles for things in your house.
On a phone held sideways, Social covered Jump, the menu and the report window were cramped, and the keyboard hid what you typed.

The pick swung beside you instead of on the rock, and a swing took about a tenth of Glitch's time. The pick now swings on the rock; the swing's length is now a third of Glitch's on purpose (see the mining pace below).
The encyclopedia did not say that some recipes, such as Wavy Gravy, need an achievement first.
Big street scenery and the Glitchmas Cracker could draw black on phones with small graphics chips.
Speech bubbles bounced back and forth on phone screens.
Adding the game to a phone's home screen opened it in the browser instead of full screen.
The Social drawer held sideways on a phone showed only its header, with no room for chat.
On an upright phone a short street left a band of plain blue above it, and the route card covered the street's name.
The start card sat off centre on a phone and always named the same first street.
The iMG button on a phone's top bar was hard to tap.
In Join the Club a good jump could clear the shut door.
Visitors could not plant, water or pick the gardens on another player's home street, which Glitch left open to everyone.
Home rocks wore out after 40 swings instead of 40 mine-outs, and a fresh restoration could refuse items at first.
The Greedy Street Spirit showed a row of seven buttons for each act instead of one.
Finding the nearest shrine could lead to a street still under construction.
The delivery frog could hide behind a vendor, and its yoga line came in a card far too big for it.
The Achievements Category list jumped back while you scrolled it.
An online Heli Kitty could fly under the grass on Marylpole Mount.
The "A new day" line arrived before the New Day screen and its fanfare.
A Feat donation counted only one stack of what you gave.
Number keys did not do emotes as they did in Glitch.
Project steps said the Focusing Orb and other tools with no wear used one wear a unit.
Dropping a tool onto a Tinkertool did not repair it, as it did in Glitch.
Friends could not help build a Tower floor, which Glitch let anyone on the floor do.
The Funpickle's Broken Teleporter could pick a street still under construction.
Speech bubbles near you slid aside and back each time you jumped.
On an iPhone the report window could sit behind the keyboard.
Dragging in Camera Mode did not move the view on an iPhone.
On a phone held upright the Menu could run off the screen without scrolling.
A report's picture at a street's end could show only the sky in Firefox.
Routes could lead through a road still under construction.
Past a street's end the mirrored scenery showed ladders and signs you could not reach.
Shake, Compress, Age and Shuck had a second More row instead of asking how many, as Glitch did.
Reports could not be edited from the phone page.
The first tutorial screen gave only a faint arrow after a few seconds, so new players did not know to pull the chain.
Ladders drawn from loose pieces had gaps between their rungs on Peatland Moors and 20 other streets.
Holding Up beside a ladder grabbed it in mid-jump; Glitch climbed only on a fresh Up press.
Phones could draw black boxes in a street's rock faces when a picture failed to reach the graphics card.
After the graphics context came back, a street's decorations stayed missing.
Password managers such as Proton Pass did not offer to fill the online sign-in in desktop Chrome.
The Chats tab showed a new-message badge for a group's "You are the only person here." note.
The Maps page squeezed each picture compare beside its words instead of running it the full width.
Asking a chicken to incubate with no egg gave the feeding line instead of Glitch's own.
The subway's stop question could take your typing while the report window was open and put you off the train.
A narrow street could be drawn stretched to the window's width when the browser kept an older copy of the page's styles.
Shrines and vendors could stand half hidden behind a foreground tree.
Subway stations were laid out stretched, with the sign too low and A Red Button off the gate box.
In Organish Chute gravity stayed upside down until you pressed Space, pinning you in a corner of the tubes.
Half of Arbor Hollow's right-hand branches pointed away from the trunk.
Ladders whose bottom hangs a little above the floor could be climbed down but not up; Glitch's reach was longer.
On some graphics cards the report picture came out black and the street map blank.
Quest cards and Pinned Quests showed only the first step of a quest with several.
Any click or key stopped a walk to a destination, where Glitch kept walking while you used the Map, chat or quests.
Holding Backspace in the chat box on a phone deleted one letter at a time.
On a phone the chat jumped up to older lines when the keyboard opened.
In the iPhone Home Screen app the Encyclopedia replaced the game with no way back.
A vendor's window stayed open after a Ticket's teleport.
On a phone a drag on Act did not move through a signpost's roads.
Rocks and other things could stand up in the trees on branches, and soil patches could hang off ledge ends.
Visiting Stones stood anywhere along a street instead of at its dead end, as in Glitch.
A bug report says Read by the team once an administrator has opened it.
Fruit trees take one pet and one water a game day and never die of neglect. Glitch wanted care about every hour, which would wilt every tree overnight here.
Crops and herbs grow about ten times faster than in Glitch, and mining and rock regrowth are sped up to match.

Mining swings take about a third of Glitch's time: 6, 4.2, 3 and 2.4 seconds for Mining I to IV, where Glitch took 20, 14, 10 and 8. Players found Glitch's pace too slow. Manic Mining still cuts the time, and energy, pick wear, xp and chunks per swing are Glitch's.
Glitch sold Teleportation tokens for real money. Nothing is for sale here, so there are no tokens, and Teleportation V gives two summons a day.
Street projects ask for a fiftieth of Glitch's amounts and pay a fiftieth of its rewards, in solo and online.
The daily quoin limit is Glitch's usual one. In its last days Glitch lifted the limit for the end of the world; the remake keeps the normal limit.
Solo play stands in for other players where it can: rival Glitches in races, companions in Feats and when helping to mine or dig, and a hired hand on street projects.
Anyone can fight the Rook. Glitch asked for Martial Imagination before you could stun it.
Rubeweed gives Luck of the Rube, which raises your chances, rather than guaranteed lucky harvests.
Machines burn fuel from their own tank instead of taking Fuel Cells from your pack.
A Plain Crystal takes one Firefly Jar and a little energy, not the seven jars Glitch's recipe asked for.
Energy and mood stop draining while the game's tab is hidden, so a forgotten background tab never runs you down. Glitch drained them whenever you were connected.

At home, on house and Tower floors, shelves and tables, a pile of the same thing has no stack limit, so emblems and moonstones pile up as high as you like. Your pack still keeps the usual stack sizes. In Glitch every pile stopped at its stack size, so emblems lay one by one and moonstones stopped at 3.
Street Piggies never starve to death. Only a Piggy you own can, if you leave it hungry.
Animals that leave a crowded street come back the next game day. In Glitch they were gone for good.
When your pack is full, a tree's harvest goes to your Magic Rock. In Glitch it stayed on the tree.
A few original sounds survive only in copies we are not free to share, so they keep a stand-in.
Badges Tiny Speck defined but never let anyone earn, such as Homesteader and The Speedhermit.
Ways to fight back against the Rook that were planned and never finished, such as a hug or a kiss leaving it open to attack.
A handful of quests Tiny Speck started and never finished or never offered.
Imagination cards that Glitch listed but that did nothing, such as Heisenberg and Potent Potions.
Artifacts with no recipe to put them together, and other items nothing in Glitch ever gave out.
More items nothing gave out: cabinets, trophy cases, a Beachball, a Paper Plane, party packs and more.
Characters only the Craftybot's catalog names, such as the Blimp, the Catch-Me-Ghost and the Letter Blocks.
Mountaineering: a climb for a party of five or more, with a permit, that was never finished.
Garden upgrades that were written but never switched on.
Two bracelets that exist in the art but that nobody could ever wear.
Eight wallpapers, floors and ceilings, such as the starry sky set, that were made but never put in the shop.
Low energy pushed the Menu off the top bar of an upright phone.
Sideways on a phone, the report window's picture buttons covered its words.
The phone street sheet had no way to open the Map.
Upright on a phone, pack search hid its results and typed letters showed late.
On a narrow screen the route card covered the pinned quests.
A vendor's Buy or Sell count had no close button on a phone.
A refused Buy with a full pack did not say why inside the shop.
Upright on a phone, Tower floors and quest rooms had a sky blue band above them.
Home machines could vanish when a home was redrawn in place.
On a phone, a pack stack dragged onto an open cabinet did not go in.
After many Acts in a row, sound effects such as the pick stopped playing.
Answering a friend's Butler after leaving their street gave an error.
A party time extension did not reach everyone's Activity.
Party Space quoins were not Glitch's party quoins.
The Map did not dim the names of streets you had not visited, as Glitch did.
Ix Completist came after seven streets instead of every Ix street.
A visited player's Tower was titled with "Your Tower" after their name.
Esc did not close the subway map at a station.
Upright on a phone, the camera showed empty space past a street's right end.
The touch stick could hardly climb ladders, and a new Up in mid-air did not grab one.
On a sideways phone, a long speech bubble ran off the top of the screen.
On a sideways phone, notices beside the avatar jumped from side to side as you walked.
Solo play had no way to report a bug.
Upright on a phone, short scenes outside towers and quest rooms still had a blue band above them.
Pack search only lit up matching stacks; Glitch listed every match under the search box, items in bags included.
There was no way to see who was on your street.
Players had no way to report another player.
Solo street projects near the start asked for nearly as much as far ones, with the same skills.
A quest room or puzzle street reached without its quest could leave you with no way out.
Sloths were a drawn stand-in instead of Tiny Speck's own sloth, its animations and its encounter.
Sloths stood on made-up trees at random spots instead of hanging in their own street's trees.
The save checker could take back things you had earned: a shrine's emblems, a donation's Gameshow Ticket, beads from a cracked Petrified Rock and some rare drops.
Today's Feat could miss quests you finished when their report didn't reach the server.
Signpost words were hard to read on phones, in a fallback serif font.
The Butler's longer hints vanished before they could be read.
A super harvest showed its bonus as "+2×", which read like a multiplier.
On some phones, speech bubbles drew thin lines out to the middle of the screen.
On an upright phone, arrival notices were drawn on top of the route card.
A party invite accepted at home refused to open the teleporter there.
The signpost hint, the Butler's bubble and the construction tag could sit over other things.
A party invite couldn't be taken from a quest room, puzzle or race; in Glitch the room waited for you and a race was given up.
The save checker took back machine output, crops, a pouch's shaken elements, rare finds and a new player's tutorial gifts.
A link to a heading on the restoration report landed far above it.
Adding parts to a tower floor had no count picker, so wall segments went all or none.
On an upright phone the subway map didn't fit and couldn't be zoomed or panned.
The restoration report's Gone for good list was empty.
A new game that skipped the tutorial started up in Hechey Track's treetops instead of on the ground.
Hub Completist badges could be earned before visiting every street of their hub.
The route arrow took a signpost from the floor below it and carried you to the next street.
Barnacles in Kalavana and Jethimadh stood on the floor instead of hanging on walls.
On an iPhone the game stopped music playing in other apps, even with its own music at 0.
A demo link or a street entered at a sideways spot could stand you in the treetops instead of on the ground.
On a phone, notices covered Act, Jump and the stick, and the quest step line covered the clock.
Online you couldn't see other players mining, digging or harvesting: Glitch showed every timed skill to the street in a thought bubble.
On an upright phone, full-screen windows stopped short of the right edge.
Reading a report, a Write to us button squeezed the report's title.
On an upright phone, the update button pushed the Menu off the top bar.
The Qurazy quoin banner covered the route card on upright phones.
On upright phones, signposts high on a street were hidden under the top bar.
Mining together didn't count for helping or the I Me Mine quest when everyone started at once. Fixed on public streets; home streets still to come.
A stack couldn't be dragged onto a Storage Display Box outside Decoration Mode.
Completist badges listed their progress as Number 58.
Making said 2 Currys instead of the item's own plural.
Some Jellisacs stood on ledges while their street's holes sat empty.
Machines in your yard refused you after coming home with the Home button.
The region map's star sat in the middle of your street instead of moving along it as you walked.
Some barnacles on Jethimadh and Kalavana streets lay on the dirt in front of their trees, and edge barnacles faced the wrong way.
The street map's arrow tab didn't expand it on a click, only on hovering.
Every street held a Musicblock that each player picked up separately; Glitch's came from drop tables and a new player's first street.
Street gardens stood anywhere on the street, two beds at most, instead of where 2012 pictures show them.
Every street had four loose Apples that Glitch never had.
Visitors didn't see what a home's owner did until they came back.
Places Glitch kept to one player, like Gentle Island and the colour levels, were shared online.
Some earned things were taken back by the save checker: the Rube Shaped Potato, artifacts, Spinning Wheel prizes, a Craftybot's work, picked-up gnomes and icons, racing Cubimals, the Funpickle.
Five World map cards showed a bare picture without their frame and name.
On the home street, the meadow and the soil stopped short of the screen edge past the house when the Social drawer was open.
A super harvest floated one number over the plot while the activity log said another.
On phones, some home street styles drew trees, rocks and hills floating above the ground.
Some speech showed a code where a less-than sign belonged.
The second and third looks of mining rocks were blurry on high-density screens.
Dragging a big pile from the floor onto a Storage Display Box moved only part of it.
Coming home from a quest kept playing the last place's music.
The map named the wrong Giant for some shrine streets, and the Rook missed a built upgrade's shrine.
The Scion of Purple was drawn blurry on computers.
Watering, hoeing and clearing could play their sound twice.
Instant Resurrection filled mood only to 100, not to your full tank.
On touch screens, dragging a stack from the pack only reached some of the places a mouse could drop it.
Feat progress could be lost when a report to the server failed.
Some routes and searches went through streets still under construction.
Some gains pushed a full energy or mood tank down, and some rewards stopped at 100 instead of your full tank.
You couldn't leave a package by dropping a stack on a friend's Butler, as Glitch allowed.
Gift wrap, mail, auctions, the Butler and other pickers sent any copy of an item, not the one you chose, so a named Cubimal or a less worn tool could be swapped.
Animals, trees and set-down things stood a little into the ground or hopped when they turned.
On phones, a quoin's amount rose behind the notices that opened at the same moment.
Words drawn in the world could switch to another font on phones.
Buy a Bag started at level 2 instead of with your first skill, as in Glitch.
In a back yard, trees could be drawn one patch over, so Wine of the Dead or a restore hit a different patch than the one you chose.
Online, a tree or animal could offer the same verb again for a moment after you used it.
A smuggling run could send you somewhere only the subway reaches, and the subway refuses smugglers.
In Camera Mode you could click a far signpost and travel without walking there.
On some streets, sky showed under the ground near the bottom of the screen.
The street map of a subway station showed only its wall and floor.
Some quest completion cards showed their rewards as plain text without icons.
On phones, item icons in the Make menu were squashed and the tool button's name spilled out.
The loading card's list of what lives on a street disappeared before you could read it.
A crab's happy or grumpy reaction to Flatter and Hug ended too soon.
